{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Partially feasible: single-column ELM resolves local (point) runoff generation — surface saturation/infiltration-excess overland flow and subsurface drainage — but cannot route or aggregate flow to a basin-integrated Naches hydrograph (no lateral connectivity in SCM mode).",
    "answerable": [
      "Point-scale surface runoff (QOVER) vs. subsurface drainage (QDRAI) partitioning at each column",
      "Snowmelt-driven runoff timing and magnitude (snowpack accumulation/ablation controls)",
      "Sensitivity of runoff to soil texture, infiltration capacity, and water-table depth",
      "Seasonal water-balance closure (P vs ET vs runoff vs storage) per column"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Basin-integrated Naches streamflow / hydrograph (requires river routing model, e.g. MOSART)",
      "Lateral groundwater/hillslope connectivity between columns",
      "Channel/floodplain processes and flow timing at gauges"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 3,
  "n_justification": "Three user-specified columns span an elevation/land-cover gradient relevant to Naches runoff: a high snow-dominated headwater near Mt. Rainier (46.85,-121.05), a mid-elevation forested/transitional site (47.02,-120.88), and a low arid shrub-steppe site (46.62,-119.90). Note the low site lies in the Columbia Basin east of the Naches watershed proper; it is retained as a warm/dry rain-dominated end-member for contrast.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "NACHES_HEADWATER_SNOW", "lat": 46.85, "lon": -121.05, "soil_texture": "loam (thin, rocky mountain soil over bedrock)"},
    {"id": "NACHES_MID_FOREST", "lat": 47.02, "lon": -120.88, "soil_texture": "sandy loam (glacial/colluvial)"},
    {"id": "COLUMBIA_ARID_STEPPE", "lat": 46.62, "lon": -119.90, "soil_texture": "silt loam (loess)"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "2000",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2014",
    "STOP_N": "15",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "2000-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QRUNOFF", "QOVER", "QDRAI", "QRGWL", "QINFL",
      "RAIN", "SNOW", "QSNOMELT", "H2OSNO", "SNOWDP", "FSNO",
      "ZWT", "SOILLIQ", "SOILICE", "TSOI", "RH2OSOI",
      "QFLX_EVAP_TOT", "FSH", "EFLX_LH_TOT", "TWS"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": ["ELM_single_column", "GSWP3_atm_forcing"],
  "assumptions": [
    "STOP_OPTION=nyears; runs use GSWP3 (CLMNCEP-style) reanalysis forcing over 2000-2014 with a preceding spin-up (accelerated + final) to equilibrate soil moisture, water table, and snowpack.",
    "Each column is an independent 1-D SCM run; no lateral/river routing (MOSART) is coupled, so results are point runoff generation, not basin discharge.",
    "Satellite/global surface datasets (PFTs, soil color, organic matter) are used at each lat/lon; user-specified soil textures noted but may differ from default surface data.",
    "The (46.62,-119.90) point is outside the topographic Naches basin and is treated as an arid end-member; drop it or relocate if strict basin coverage is required.",
    "Sub-daily history output (e.g., hourly QOVER/QSNOMELT) recommended for melt-driven runoff timing; monthly default assumed unless refined."
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: single-column ELM resolves local (point) runoff generation — surface saturation/infiltration-excess overland flow and subsurface drainage — but cannot route or aggregate flow to a basin-integrated Naches hydrograph (no lateral connectivity in SCM mode).
answerable: Point-scale surface runoff (QOVER) vs. subsurface drainage (QDRAI) partitioning at each column
Snowmelt-driven runoff timing and magnitude (snowpack accumulation/ablation controls)
Sensitivity of runoff to soil texture, infiltration capacity, and water-table depth
Seasonal water-balance closure (P vs ET vs runoff vs storage) per column
not_answerable: Basin-integrated Naches streamflow / hydrograph (requires river routing model, e.g. MOSART)
Channel/floodplain processes and flow timing at gauges

parsed.n_justification: Three user-specified columns span an elevation/land-cover gradient relevant to Naches runoff: a high snow-dominated headwater near Mt. Rainier (46.85,-121.05), a mid-elevation forested/transitional site (47.02,-120.88), and a low arid shrub-steppe site (46.62,-119.90). Note the low site lies in the Columbia Basin east of the Naches watershed proper; it is retained as a warm/dry rain-dominated end-member for contrast.

columns.soil_texture: loam (thin, rocky mountain soil over bedrock)

assumptions: STOP_OPTION=nyears; runs use GSWP3 (CLMNCEP-style) reanalysis forcing over 2000-2014 with a preceding spin-up (accelerated + final) to equilibrate soil moisture, water table, and snowpack.
Each column is an independent 1-D SCM run; no lateral/river routing (MOSART) is coupled, so results are point runoff generation, not basin discharge.
Satellite/global surface datasets (PFTs, soil color, organic matter) are used at each lat/lon; user-specified soil textures noted but may differ from default surface data.
The (46.62,-119.90) point is outside the topographic Naches basin and is treated as an arid end-member; drop it or relocate if strict basin coverage is required.
Sub-daily history output (e.g., hourly QOVER/QSNOMELT) recommended for melt-driven runoff timing; monthly default assumed unless refined.
